# Contact form → email to support@tillsa.app

Sender domain `notify.tillsa.app` is verified and auth emails already run through it. What's missing is the app-email side (templates + send route), so step 1 scaffolds that once.

## Files

**Scaffolded (generated by the app-email setup, then styled by me)**
- `src/lib/email-templates/registry.ts` — new template registry
- `src/routes/lovable/email/transactional/send.ts` — authenticated send route
- `src/routes/lovable/email/transactional/preview.ts` — dashboard preview
- `src/routes/email/unsubscribe.ts` + branded unsubscribe page — created by scaffolding
- `src/routes/lovable/email/suppression.ts`

**New**
- `src/lib/email-templates/contact-form.tsx` — the "contact_form" email: brand-styled, shows submitter name, email, message. Subject: `New contact message from {name}`. Recipient fixed to `support@tillsa.app`.
- `src/routes/api/public/contact.ts` — public POST endpoint. Contact submitters are not logged in, so the authenticated send route can't be called from the browser; this route validates input, applies abuse protection, then sends internally with service credentials. Sets `replyTo` to the submitter's email.
- `src/routes/contact.tsx` — marketing page modelled on `about.tsx` (MarketingHeader + hero + form card + MarketingFooter, per-language head meta, canonical `https://tillsa.app/contact`).

**Edited**
- `src/components/carenest/MarketingFooter.tsx` — "Contact" becomes a `/contact` route link; `CONTACT_EMAIL` const removed (only used for that mailto; `about.tsx` has its own copy and is untouched).
- `src/lib/i18n/en.ts` / `src/lib/i18n/sv.ts` — `marketing.contact.*` keys: page meta, heading, intro, field labels/placeholders, validation messages, submit button, success state, error state. Exact parity.
- `package.json` / `vite.config.ts` — only if scaffolding needs email packages that aren't installed yet.

## Reply-To

The email is sent from an `@notify.tillsa.app` sender to `support@tillsa.app` with `Reply-To: <submitter email>`, so replying in Proton reaches the customer. If the send path turns out not to expose a reply-to field, I'll say so instead of silently shipping without it — and fall back to putting the submitter address prominently at the top of the body.

## Abuse protection (chosen, no CAPTCHA)

1. **Honeypot** — a visually hidden `website` field; any non-empty value returns a fake success and sends nothing.
2. **Time trap** — form render timestamp; submissions faster than ~3 seconds are dropped as bot traffic.
3. **In-memory per-IP rate limit** — max 3 submissions per IP per 10 minutes in the public route, returning 429 with a friendly message. In-memory means it resets on worker recycle; that's acceptable for a low-volume contact form and needs no DB table (which is out of scope).
4. **Strict zod validation** — name ≤ 100, email format ≤ 255, message 10–5000 chars; everything escaped by React in the template (no raw HTML).

## Verification

`/contact` in both languages, footer link (no mailto), success + error states, en/sv key parity, `tsgo --noEmit` clean. Real inbox delivery to Proton is yours to confirm after.
